title: a Totally Normal Vanilla+ Modpack
description: a Totally Normal Vanilla+ Modpack that focuses on improving and adding features instead of adding random content, based on exploration and QoL.
body:
# a Totally Normal Vanilla+ Modpack

a Totally Normal Vanilla+ Modpack is, as its name suggests, **a Totally Normal Vanilla+ Modpack**.

## Information
Originally created for me and my friends, I wanted to share it with others looking for the same Vanilla+ style I tried to create.

This Modpack aims to "upgrade" the vanilla experience. It focuses on immersion, QoL and a global overhaul of the game. I tried to add as few items and mobs as possible (with some exception). There are optimization mods installed, but they mostly compensate for the performance impact of the other mods, you will probably not see a huge performance increase (or any performance increase at all).

It also have 8 resource packs (not counting the mods ones) that you can use.

## Which version to use?

The modpack come in 2 versions, so choosing the right one is always a plus!

- **The Classic Version**: The classic version (named aTNV+M Vx.x) use Vulkan since V1.0 and Rust + OpenCL since V1.3, this version is not compatible with every computer. Use this version if your PC is compatible and Beryl shader is good enough for you.

- **The Sodium Version**: The sodium version (named aTNV+M Vx.x-Sodium) use Sodium instead of Vulkan and does not use Rust or OpenCL, this version is the most compatible one. Use this version if your PC is not compatible or if you want more shader and DH support.

(The latest posted version is the V1.3, idk if there any delay :P)

More versions will (probably) come in the future.

## Q&A

### Why should I use this modpack?

You can use this modpack for having a better Vanilla experience without finishing in the thousands of modded items and mobs. You can also use this modpack as a base for your personal or published modpack (just please mark that you used this modpack as a base in your description if you're publishing it) since it almost doesn't add any items or mobs.

### How can I play with my friends?

You can play with your friends by hosting (if you're the host) or joining your friend World. What the Host need to do is create a SinglePlayer World, once in the World press Open to LAN, the host will receive a server address and the port (not important except if the host is blocking port for unblocking it), then the host can share it to his friends. Now they can play together!


### Who should Host the World?

The Host should be the one who have the strongest PC. If you all have good PC, then the one with the most stable connection should Host.


### How do I (the creator) test the Modpack?

I test the classic version on my personal PC (for more details, check the Note section below). I test every mod I add (since V1.3, I know, it's a little late and I test it in creative mode) before deciding to put it or not in the Modpack.

### Did I (the creator) have inspiration from Modpack?

Yes, you can check it in the Note section below (also you should try them!).

### What mod and resource pack this modpack contains?

You can check it in the Note section below


### Why are there deactivated mods?

The deactivated mods are optional. For example, Controllable is a deactivated mod because not everyone play Minecraft on a controller, so instead of making everyone have this mod activated, the ones who want to play Minecraft on a controller can activate this mod (don't forget Framework tho).

### What resources packs order should I use?

For the resources packs order, you can use this one (from bottom to top): Minecraft, True Ending: Ender Dragon Music, Default Connected Textures, Glass Pane Culling Fix, Sparkles, Fresh Animations, FA+All Extensions, Animated Items, GUIRetextures, Os' Colorful Grasses, Simple Grass Flowers, Cursors Extended.

### How much RAM should I Allocate (Solo)?

Allocating 4GB of RAM for Minecraft should be enough, the modpack consume ~1-2GB of RAM.

### Why do I get random lag spike (even without exploring)?

The lag spike is likely caused by the Garbage Collection (GC) which I can't fix, you need to set the best JVM arguments for your computer (don't put random generic arguments found online).
